extracted.intended_audience: press, media and communications officers at universities, research institutes, and similar organisations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for press officers on working with the Science Media Centre to support scientists/engineers during breaking, controversial, or complex science stories and to propose/organise briefings. Covers when SMC will help, how to propose experts/briefings, and practical policies (expert inclusion, contact preferences, training, and limits of SMC services).

rubrics_metrics.name: SMC role and independence
rubrics_metrics.description: The Science Media Centre can provide a neutral venue when your organisation wants to speak out alongside other experts, or act as a central coordination point on key issues. As an independent organisation without any institutional brand name or agenda, we are genuine partners in the effort to help your experts engage with the media when it matters most.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SMC positions itself as an independent coordinator and neutral convenor, able to host briefings, coordinate third-party expert quotes, and help shape responses on significant scientific, health or environmental stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert database inclusion policy
rubrics_metrics.description: We generally don’t add experts before we’ve worked with them at least once
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You are encouraged to put experts in touch with SMC for a quote or interview; if that goes well SMC may add them to the database for future contact. Prior direct working relationship with SMC is normally required before formal inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactivity for breaking stories
rubrics_metrics.description: When a story breaks we will usually email a large group to request quotes. But we can’t guarantee we’ll reach everyone! So the best advice is, don’t wait to hear from us; if you have an expert who can contribute usefully to the story, let us know!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Press officers should proactively alert SMC to available experts during breaking news rather than relying solely on SMC outreach; this increases chance of media engagement and placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of expert use
rubrics_metrics.description: Can you tell me when you use one of our experts? — We do our best to alert you every time we work with your experts, and we ask them to let you know too.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SMC aims to inform institutional press officers when their experts are engaged, but this is not guaranteed; encourage experts to notify their press officers as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for direct contact with experts
rubrics_metrics.description: We prefer to contact experts directly because we usually need to respond fast – we’re not trying to undermine you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most press officers accept direct contact because speed matters. If a press officer prefers being contacted first they should tell SMC, but be aware that any delay can affect how accurately a story is covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Briefing eligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Please do contact us if you think you have a story we could work together on, providing it falls into one of the following categories: Big, breaking science stories that are the headline news of the day; Controversial, messy, or politicised scientific issues; New scientific studies that may be sensationalised, overplayed or misrepresented; Issues where the scientific community wants to speak out as one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Briefings are typically selected when they meet one or more of these public-interest/impact categories. Press officers should assess whether a proposed topic fits these criteria before pitching a briefing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance notice and communication limits
rubrics_metrics.description: There’s just no way we can alert all press officers to every briefing they might find interesting and we often only have a few days’ notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect comprehensive advance notice; if a briefing concerns your institution SMC will try to inform you, but timelines are often short so maintain active communication channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speaker selection for briefings
rubrics_metrics.description: The briefings in your monthly report always have speakers already arranged – we don’t get a look in! ... For background briefings we like to have speakers from a variety of institutions, so if you have an expert working in a particularly important or controversial area, please let us know
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many news briefings feature authors or pre-arranged speakers; background briefings aim for institutional variety. Press officers should offer suitably experienced experts to increase chances of inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working with SMC on controversial issues
rubrics_metrics.description: We specialise in controversial areas and we’re always keen to work on them. We can often help with the response: whether it’s dealing with a breaking story, placing an opinion piece, briefing the press on a sensitive piece of research, putting the spotlight on an important issue, or issuing quotes from 3rd party experts alongside your press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SMC can help craft coordinated responses, arrange briefings, place commentary, and provide third-party expert quotes; contact them early (even for background or advice) for best results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science communication training availability
rubrics_metrics.description: We don’t provide traditional media training, mainly because most universities and research councils already do. We run our Introduction to the News Media events, which are free and introduce inexperienced scientists and engineers to news values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SMC offers introductory events for inexperienced scientists but defers formal media training to institutions and established training providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training recommendation for press officers
rubrics_metrics.description: We don’t offer any training for press officers but we would strongly recommend that you join Stempra, an informal network ... They run events, training and an online forum to share questions and concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Press officers should consider Stempra membership for peer networking, events, and professional training rather than relying on SMC for press-officer-specific training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior-expert expectation for briefings
rubrics_metrics.description: We have a PhD student doing some really interesting work – could we run a press briefing? — Probably not! ... the most controversial headline subjects ... generally demand more experienced experts from at least postdoc level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Press officers should prioritise postdocs or more senior researchers for briefings on high-profile or controversial topics; PhD students are unlikely to be appropriate in those contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for scientist/engineer quotes vs spokespeople
rubrics_metrics.description: Can we send you a comment from our spokesperson / manager / head of policy / head of comms? — Usually not. It’s occasionally ok, under certain circumstances ... But in general it is only scientists/engineers we want for quotes on research papers and breaking news – so best to check with us first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SMC generally prefers technical/scientific voices for quotes linked to research and breaking science stories; organizational spokespeople may be acceptable only for broader stories with room for many voices.

rubrics_metrics.name: No distribution of press releases or sharing journalist lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Can you send out a press release for us, or share your journalist lists with us? — No, we don’t send out press releases as we can’t do other organisations’ PR. We also do not share our journalist lists, but we do notify you about specialist journalists moving jobs etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SMC will not perform third-party PR distribution nor disclose its journalist contacts; press officers should manage their own release distribution and use SMC for coordination/briefings rather than PR services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert billing and affiliation changes policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Please can you use a particular title/affiliation for our experts? — We don’t want to get this wrong ... we ask the expert how he/she wants to be billed. If you want someone’s affiliation changed in this way, please copy in the expert when you let us know so we can get their direct permission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always include the expert in requests to alter their displayed title/affiliation so SMC can obtain direct permission and avoid misattribution.
